questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In Re Berubari Union (1960), the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is:

options.A: A source of substantive power for Parliament
options.B: A part of the Constitution and enforceable
options.C: A limitation on the amending power
options.D: Not a part of the Constitution

questions.explanation: Berubari treated the Preamble as a key to the mind of the framers but not part of the Constitution; Kesavananda overruled this.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added to the Preamble by the:
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment is often called the 'mini-Constitution'.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: For the purposes of Article 13, the term 'law' includes:

options.A: Only laws made by Parliament or State Legislatures
options.C: Ordinances, bye-laws and customs with force of law
options.D: Only judgments of the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Article 13(3)(a) gives an inclusive definition covering ordinances, orders, bye-laws, rules, regulations, notifications, custom or usage.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Untouchability is abolished and its practice forbidden in any form by:
questions.explanation: Article 17 is enforced through the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In Nandini Satpathy v. P.L. Dani, the Supreme Court held that Article 20(3) extends to:

options.A: Questioning by the police during investigation
options.B: Only witnesses who are not accused
options.C: Only confessions made before a magistrate in court
options.D: Only statements made in a court trial

questions.explanation: The right against self-incrimination applies from the stage of interrogation, and the accused may remain silent.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Freedom of the press was read into Article 19(1)(a) in:

options.A: Chintaman Rao v. State of M.P. (1950)
options.B: Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras (1950)
options.C: Ranjit Udeshi v. State of Maharashtra (1965)
options.D: State of Madras v. V.G. Row (1952)

questions.explanation: The Court struck down a ban on circulation of a journal as violating freedom of speech and expression.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In Shamsher Singh v. State of Punjab, the Supreme Court held that the President and Governor ordinarily act on:

options.A: The advice of the Chief Justice
options.B: Their own personal discretion in all matters of State
options.C: The orders of the Election Commission
options.D: The aid and advice of the Council of Ministers

questions.explanation: The President and Governors are constitutional heads, except in matters where the Constitution gives discretion.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Unlike the President, the Governor under Article 161 cannot grant:

options.B: A pardon of a sentence of death
options.D: A remission of the whole sentence

questions.explanation: The Governor can suspend, remit or commute a death sentence, but only the President can pardon it.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Article 129 declares the Supreme Court to be:
questions.explanation: A court of record has power to punish for its own contempt.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Control over district courts and courts subordinate to them is vested by Article 235 in:
questions.explanation: Article 235 secures the independence of the subordinate judiciary from the executive.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: A joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament under Article 108 is presided over by the:
questions.explanation: A joint sitting resolves a deadlock on an ordinary Bill; it cannot be held for Money Bills or Constitution Amendment Bills.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The right to live with human dignity, including protection against bonded labour, was affirmed under Article 21 in:

options.B: Lily Thomas v. Union of India
options.C: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
options.D: Mohd. Ahmed Khan v. Shah Bano Begum

questions.explanation: The Court linked Article 21 with Directive Principles to define the minimum conditions of a dignified life.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The majority in ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla (1976), later declared wrong in Puttaswamy, held that during an Emergency:

options.B: Parliament could not suspend any right
options.C: Enforcement of Article 21 could be suspended
options.D: Courts retained full power to review detention

questions.explanation: The Puttaswamy Bench described ADM Jabalpur as seriously flawed.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The realist theory of corporate personality, treating a group as a real entity, is associated with:
questions.explanation: Savigny's fiction theory holds that corporate personality is a legal fiction; Gierke held a group has a real will.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The labour theory of property is associated with:
questions.explanation: Locke argued that mixing labour with unowned things creates property rights.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The reformative theory of punishment emphasises:
questions.explanation: It treats crime as a social disease and aims at the reform of the criminal.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: For Austin, the sovereign is a determinate human superior who:

options.A: Receives habitual obedience and obeys no one
options.D: Is bound by natural law and morality

questions.explanation: Austin's sovereign is legally unlimited and is the source of command.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: Rights over a person's own property, such as ownership, are called:
questions.explanation: Proprietary rights relate to property; personal rights relate to a person's status, body or reputation.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The 'entitlement theory' of justice and the idea of the minimal State are associated with:
questions.explanation: Nozick's Anarchy, State, and Utopia defends a libertarian view.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The theory of 'social solidarity' in law was propounded by:
questions.explanation: Duguit rejected natural rights and said law rests on the social fact of interdependence.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: In Lalman Shukla v. Gauri Dutt, the claimant could not recover the reward because he:

options.A: Was not a resident of that town at the time
options.C: Had already been paid by another person
options.D: Acted without knowledge of the offer

questions.explanation: Acceptance of a general offer requires knowledge of the offer.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: In Felthouse v. Bindley, the court held that:

options.C: Acceptance may validly be made by silence
options.D: Silence cannot be imposed as acceptance

questions.explanation: The offeror cannot make the offeree's silence an acceptance.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: In Balfour v. Balfour, agreements between spouses for domestic arrangements were held to:

options.A: Be voidable at the wife's option
options.C: Lack intention to create legal relations
options.D: Be void for want of any lawful consideration

questions.explanation: Social and domestic agreements are presumed not to be intended as legally binding.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under the Indian Majority Act, 1875, a person ordinarily attains majority at:

options.A: 21 years in all cases, irrespective of guardian
options.B: 18 years, or 21 if a guardian was appointed

questions.explanation: Under the Act, majority is 18 years, but 21 where a guardian of person or property has been appointed by a court.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 16 of the Contract Act, undue influence exists where one party is in a position to:

options.A: Dominate the will of the other
options.D: Give a large gift to the other party

questions.explanation: The dominant party uses that position to obtain an unfair advantage.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 24 of the Contract Act, where part of the object is unlawful and cannot be separated, the agreement is:

options.C: Void only for the unlawful promisor

questions.explanation: If the lawful and unlawful parts can be severed, the lawful part may be enforced.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: A contract by which one party promises to save the other from loss caused by the promisor's own conduct is:
questions.explanation: Section 124 defines the contract of indemnity.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Battery in tort consists of:

options.A: Interference with the use and enjoyment of land
options.B: Intentional application of force to a person
options.C: Mere threat of immediate harm without contact

questions.explanation: Assault is the threat; battery is the actual contact.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Conversion in tort means:

options.A: Transfer of goods by lawful sale
options.B: Damage caused to land by a neighbour

questions.explanation: It is an act of deliberate dealing with another's goods inconsistent with his rights of ownership.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: In Sturges v. Bridgman, the court held that 'coming to the nuisance' is:

options.B: A defence if the plaintiff consented

questions.explanation: A defendant cannot claim that the plaintiff moved in after the nuisance began.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: The 'last opportunity' rule in negligence arose in:
questions.explanation: The donkey case held that the party with the last clear chance to avoid harm bears the loss.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: In occupiers' liability, a person who enters premises for the occupier's business and benefit is called:
questions.explanation: Indermaur v. Dames held that the occupier owes invitees a duty to prevent unusual danger.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: In defamation, an 'innuendo' is:

options.A: A privileged report of court proceedings
options.B: A formal apology offered by the defendant in court
options.C: A hidden defamatory meaning known to some readers
options.D: A statement that is true in substance

questions.explanation: A true or legal innuendo must be pleaded with the special facts known to the readers.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Stalking is dealt with in which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 78 corresponds to Section 354D IPC; Section 77 deals with voyeurism.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Causing grievous hurt by use of acid is punishable under which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 124 replaces Sections 326A and 326B IPC.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Theft or extortion becomes 'robbery' when the offender causes or attempts to cause:

options.C: Annoyance or insult to the owner

questions.explanation: Robbery is defined in Section 309 BNS.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Dacoity is committed when robbery is committed or attempted by:
questions.explanation: Section 310 BNS corresponds to Section 391 IPC.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Criminal breach of trust is defined in which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 316 corresponds to Section 405 IPC.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Rioting under the BNS requires force or violence used by:

options.B: An unlawful assembly or any member of it
options.D: A single individual in a public place

questions.explanation: Rioting is committed when an unlawful assembly or its member uses force or violence in prosecution of its common object.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: A person abets an offence if he instigates it, engages in a conspiracy for it, or:
questions.explanation: Abetment requires instigation, conspiracy or intentional aid, not mere knowledge.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Under the BNS, kidnapping from lawful guardianship applies to a female child under the age of:
questions.explanation: For a male child, the age is sixteen years.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Order VIII Rule 1 CPC, a written statement must be filed within thirty days, extendable at most up to:

options.A: Ninety days from service of summons
options.C: Sixty days from service of summons

questions.explanation: Courts have no power to extend time beyond ninety days for ordinary suits.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Section 89 of the CPC empowers the court to refer disputes for:

options.A: Only trial by a commissioner appointed by court
options.C: Only summary disposal without a full hearing
options.D: Arbitration, conciliation, mediation or Lok Adalat

questions.explanation: Section 89 promotes settlement outside court, as explained in Salem Advocate Bar Association.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Section 92 of the CPC allows a suit relating to a public charitable trust to be filed by:

options.A: The Advocate General or two persons with leave
options.C: Any police officer on a complaint of mismanagement
options.D: The Registrar of the High Court

questions.explanation: It prevents frivolous suits about public trusts.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: The High Court can exercise revisional jurisdiction under Section 115 CPC in cases decided by subordinate courts with:

options.A: A finding of fact against a party
options.C: An error in appreciation of evidence
options.D: A decree of the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Revision is limited to jurisdictional errors, such as exercise of jurisdiction not vested or failure to exercise it.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: A suit by or against one or more persons on behalf of numerous persons with the same interest under Order I Rule 8 is a:
questions.explanation: Notice must be given to all interested persons.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Section 479 of the BNSS, a first-time offender undergoing trial is entitled to bail after serving:
questions.explanation: Other undertrials are entitled after serving one-half of the maximum sentence.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Section 18 of the Limitation Act, a fresh period of limitation begins from:

options.A: An oral promise to pay the debt later
options.C: A signed written acknowledgment of liability
options.D: A notice sent by the creditor

questions.explanation: The acknowledgment must be made before the original period expires.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Section 3 of the Limitation Act, a time-barred suit must be dismissed:

options.B: Only if the defendant pleads limitation
options.C: Even if limitation is not set up as a defence

questions.explanation: The bar of limitation is mandatory and operates on the court.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Facts forming part of the same transaction, even if not in issue, are relevant under the doctrine of:
questions.explanation: Section 6 of the Evidence Act (Section 4 BSA) codifies res gestae.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: In criminal proceedings, the fact that the accused is of good character is:

options.A: Relevant only if the prosecution proves it

questions.explanation: Section 53 makes good character relevant; bad character is irrelevant unless it is itself a fact in issue or good character is raised.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Under Section 113B of the Evidence Act, the court shall presume dowry death if the woman was subjected to cruelty:

options.C: At any time during the marriage

questions.explanation: The presumption also requires that cruelty or harassment be for, or in connection with, a demand for dowry.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: The standard of proof required in criminal trials is:
questions.explanation: The accused is entitled to the benefit of reasonable doubt.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: India follows the dualist approach to treaties, because treaties are domestically enforceable only after:

options.A: Ratification by all the States of the Union
options.B: Prior approval of the Supreme Court of India

questions.explanation: Article 253 enables Parliament to legislate to implement treaties.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The International Court of Justice consists of how many judges?
questions.explanation: Judges are elected for nine-year terms by the General Assembly and Security Council.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The Exclusive Economic Zone extends up to:
questions.explanation: Under UNCLOS Article 57, the coastal State has sovereign rights over resources in the EEZ.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The doctrine of 'rebus sic stantibus' relates to termination of treaties due to:

options.A: Breach of diplomatic immunity by an envoy
options.D: Death of a head of State

questions.explanation: Article 62 of the Vienna Convention allows this only in narrow circumstances.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: Under Article 31 of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, a diplomatic agent enjoys:

options.D: No immunity from civil jurisdiction at all

questions.explanation: The sending State may waive the immunity.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: Hot pursuit of a foreign ship by the coastal State may begin when the ship is within the:

options.C: Territorial sea of a third State
options.D: Internal waters, territorial sea or contiguous zone

questions.explanation: Article 111 of UNCLOS: pursuit must be continuous and ends once the ship enters the territorial sea of its own or another State.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: Under the Hindu Marriage Act, sapinda relationship extends up to how many generations on the mother's side?
questions.explanation: On the father's side it extends to five generations.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: The manager of a Hindu joint family is called the:
questions.explanation: The Karta manages family property and affairs.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: In Muslim law, 'hizanat' means:
questions.explanation: A mother is entitled to the custody of a young child, but guardianship generally remains with the father.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: Section 41 of the TPA protects a transferee who relies on the title of:

options.A: An ostensible owner with the owner's consent
options.C: A trespasser in wrongful possession of land

questions.explanation: The transferee must have taken reasonable care and acted in good faith.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: Under Section 53 of the TPA, a transfer made to defeat or delay creditors is:

options.B: Valid for all purposes against creditors
options.D: Voidable at the option of the creditors

questions.explanation: A transfer for consideration and in good faith is protected.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: The mortgagor's right to recover the mortgaged property on payment of the debt is the right of:
questions.explanation: Section 60 TPA gives the mortgagor the right to redeem, which cannot be defeated by a clog on redemption.

questions.subject: Intellectual Property Law
questions.question: Under Section 3(k) of the Patents Act, 1970, which of the following is not patentable as such?
questions.explanation: Computer programmes per se, mathematical methods and algorithms are excluded.

questions.subject: Environmental Law
questions.question: The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 empowers State Governments to declare:
questions.explanation: State Boards can then regulate industries in such areas.

questions.subject: Company Law
questions.question: A company with only one member is called, under the Companies Act, 2013, a:
questions.explanation: Section 2(62) defines OPC; it must be a private company.

questions.subject: Banking Law
questions.question: The SARFAESI Act, 2002 allows secured creditors to enforce security interest:

options.C: Only through a civil court decree
options.D: Without the intervention of a court

questions.explanation: Banks can take possession of the secured assets after notice under Section 13.

questions.subject: Competition Law
questions.question: Under Section 3 of the Competition Act, 2002, an agreement among competitors to fix prices is presumed to have:

options.A: A reasonable restraint of trade effect
options.B: The effect of an unnotified merger
options.C: A lawful and beneficial trade effect
options.D: An appreciable adverse effect on competition

questions.explanation: Cartels are subject to the presumption of appreciable adverse effect on competition.

questions.subject: Consumer Law
questions.question: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a person who buys goods for a commercial purpose is:

options.A: A consumer if goods exceed ₹1 lakh

questions.explanation: An exception exists for goods bought exclusively for livelihood by self-employment.

questions.subject: Administrative Law
questions.question: The Lokpal under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 consists of a Chairperson and not more than:
questions.explanation: Fifty per cent of the members must be judicial members.

questions.subject: Arbitration Law
questions.question: Under Section 29A of the Arbitration Act, an award must be made within twelve months, extendable by consent of parties by:
questions.explanation: Beyond that, the court may extend the time on sufficient cause.

questions.subject: Intellectual Property Law
questions.question: A trade mark is 'deceptively similar' to another if it is likely to:

options.C: Reduce the cost of the goods
options.D: Increase the sales of the goods

questions.explanation: Section 2(1)(h) of the Trade Marks Act, 1999 defines deceptive similarity.

questions.subject: Environmental Law
questions.question: The Chairperson of the National Green Tribunal must be:

options.A: A retired senior civil servant of the Union
options.B: A Union Minister of Environment and Forests
options.C: A sitting or retired Judge of the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Section 4 of the NGT Act, 2010 prescribes this qualification (or a Chief Justice of a High Court).
